title: Chess Piece Shadow Theater Simulator
description: Users direct a spotlight over a chess set (ABeautifulGame) placed on a shadow-receiving stage (ShadowmappableMesh), casting dramatic real-time shadows. By adjusting light angle, intensity, color temperature, height, and cone angle, users compose theatrical shadow scenes and capture snapshots graded on shadow coverage and drama.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads ABeautifulGame.glb (a full chess set) and ShadowmappableMesh.glb (used as a flat shadow-receiving stage/floor beneath and behind the chess pieces). Set up a perspective camera at position (0, 8, 12) looking at the origin. Use OrbitControls for camera navigation. Enable the renderer's shadow map with PCFSoftShadowMap type. Place the chess set centered at the origin on top of the ShadowmappableMesh, which should be scaled to act as a large stage floor (scale ~5x). Ensure the stage mesh has receiveShadow=true and all chess piece meshes have castShadow=true. Add a single SpotLight (white, intensity 50, positioned at (5, 10, 5)) with castShadow=true, shadow map size 2048x2048, and a visible SpotLightHelper. Add dim ambient light (intensity 0.15). Build a GUI panel (HTML/CSS overlay, no dat.gui) with these interactive controls: (1) a circular angle slider (0-360°) that orbits the spotlight around the chess set at its current height, (2) a vertical slider for light height (2-20 units), (3) an intensity slider (10-100), (4) a cone angle slider (Math.PI/8 to Math.PI/3) controlling the spot penumbra spread, (5) a color temperature selector with preset buttons: Warm (0xFFAA55), Cool (0x88BBFF), Neutral (0xFFFFFF), Dramatic Red (0xFF3333), (6) a 'Capture Shadow Scene' button that evaluates the current configuration. When captured, validate that: light height is between 2-20, intensity is 10-100, cone angle is in valid range, and the spotlight target is the chess set origin. Display a score (0-100) based on how oblique the light angle is (lower height = longer shadows = higher drama score) combined with intensity. Show the score in a styled overlay that fades after 3 seconds. Update the SpotLightHelper each frame. The spotlight should always point at (0, 0, 0). Use an animation loop for continuous rendering.
